text:
olivia: follow-up from RFC review: proposing a compact service-auth surface focusing on three operations: (1) create-scoped-key, (2) mint-ephemeral, (3) revoke/session-list. want to confirm API ergonomics and threat model.
kevin: sounds good. prefer explicit verbs in the API. create-scoped-key should require scope parameter and an optional human-readable reason. default scope = project unless caller specifies scope=org and has org-admin rights.
sasha: +1. small caveat: we need a machine-friendly path for infra that creates many org-scoped keys via tooling. recommend a service-account-only endpoint that enforces MFA/approval and logs requestor identity.
maria: threat model: long-lived keys must not carry high-privilege roles (no full-admin). enforce a validation rule at creation time and reject if role in payload is in denylist or needs SSO approval.
dan: about mint-ephemeral: broker should accept a list of requested_claims and return a token and metadata { ttl, issued_for, parent_key } in the response. include an issued_token_id for revocation.
olivia: want to require proof-of-possession for minting when using a long-lived key: HMAC signing of the mint request to prevent third-party reuse. reduces stolen-key replay.
sasha: operational tradeoff: PoP increases client complexity but worthwhile for high-value org keys. we can make it opt-in but recommended for org-scope keys.
maria: logging: every mint needs to emit audit event with grant predicate, decision, and optional approver id. also mark token_source as "long-lived" or "broker" for downstream telemetry.
kevin: how do we revoke? thinking of two axes: revoke by issued_token_id (single token) and revoke-by-parent (revoke all tokens minted from a parent key). plus ability to revoke by claimant (svc id). console should show active sessions and allow targeted revocation.
dan: implement revoke list and publish via sidecar to runtime nodes. runtimes subscribe to revocation stream and check cache. keep streaming heartbeat to avoid long revocation windows.
olivia: cache TTL on runtimes should be tunable but default 30s to 2m. provide hooks to force immediate revalidation for critical endpoints.
sasha: concerning RBAC resolution: propose deterministic rule set: exact project claim wins, otherwise org claim wins, otherwise fall back to resource ACL. publish this precedence in docs and tests.
maria: add tests: create matrix that includes tokens with overlapping claims and assert allow/deny for read/write/admin verbs across projects. run in CI gate.
kevin: migration plan for existing keys: don't expire immediately. enable a "scoped-keys-only" feature flag per org. when flag on, API creation without scope fails. run shadow-check for 45 days and surface top 20 legacy keys by usage.
olivia: UI/CLI UX: when creating key, CLI should prompt for scope if omitted (interactive) and require --scope=org explicit flag for org-scoped keys in scripts. API returns 400 if ambiguous.
dan: consider backcompat header: X-Allow-Legacy-Keys for internal infra tooling during migration window; gated by org feature flag and logs usage.
sasha: impersonation flows: allow broker to mint a one-off project-scoped token for org-scoped caller if they present an approval token. approvals can be: signed grant (org-admin), time-limited owner token, or pre-registered delegation policy. log every impersonation and require two approver types for >24h TTL.
maria: limit impersonation endpoints to a small set of routes. mark them in router so we can add extra monitoring and alerts if abuse is suspected.
kevin: action items:
- dan: implement simple revocation stream + issued_token_id in broker prototype (ETA 2w)
- olivia: draft CLI UX & API param spec + examples (ETA 1w)
- sasha: add RBAC precedence section + test matrix to auth model doc (ETA 1w)
- maria: build audit-event schema for mint/revoke/impersonation (ETA 1w)
auth-bot: created ticket INF-4380 assigned to dan (service-auth broker revocation prototype)
kevin: question: do we enforce PoP for all org keys after migration?
maria: recommend opt-in initially, then evaluate telemetry and decide at end of pilot. PoP by default for admin-ish scopes.
sasha: one last note: make sure SDKs can do PoP without exposing secrets; use ephemeral signing keys rotated by the SDK runtime.
dan: will prototype with a small client lib.
olivia: thanks all, scheduling a 30m sync next Wed to review the prototype and UX. :calendar:
kevin: thanks. closing thread.
